title: NTT Smile Energy says attackers breached its Eco Megane solar monitoring service and points were fraudulently exchanged
date_note: Publication date of Security NEXT; the company spotted the access on October 28.
summary: NTT Smile Energy, which runs the Eco Megane solar remote monitoring service, detected suspicious external access to its web server on October 28. Log analysis showed a software vulnerability was exploited, with traces on the customer database server. Customer names, contact details and login credentials may have leaked, and Smile e-Points were fraudulently exchanged for gift codes. About 14,000 fraudulent exchanges totalling 8 million points were reported.
plain: A Japanese solar monitoring service was hacked; customer details may be exposed and loyalty points were stolen.
exec: Customer credentials and points were exposed through a web vulnerability at an energy-service provider.
action: Customers should change reused Eco Megane passwords and watch for phishing; operators should patch internet-facing web servers.

validation.note: Security NEXT (Japanese) read in full; the number affected is not stated.

review.note: Facts match Security NEXT; added the reported 14,000 fraudulent exchanges and 8 million points, fixed exec grammar
